night_cron.description: 6-field Quartz cron of the nightly close sweep, declared in UTC (KEEPER_NIGHT_CRON). The default is the UTC image of 00:00-06:00 Europe/Berlin in SUMMER (CEST, UTC+2): 22:00-03:30 UTC, twelve firings every thirty minutes. Winter (CET, UTC+1) is '0 0,30 23,0-4 * * *'. Compute your own: UTC = local - offset.

description.purpose: The night of the keeper. It fires every thirty minutes through the local night and asks the close pass one question each time: is any channel silent enough to end its session? It sends, it does not decide -- schedule_name is what the close pass recognises as a firing.
description.use_when: Inside the session-keeper hive. Change the window at runtime with add/modify/remove ops by schedule_id, or once at instantiation via KEEPER_NIGHT_CRON.
description.not_in_scope: No catch-up: a missed firing is dropped by design, and it costs nothing -- the next firing thirty minutes later finds the same idle channel. No judgement about sessions; the timer knows nothing about channels.
description.emits_meaning: hop.schedule_name = 'night-close' is the marker the close pass gates its sweep on; the body is a plain trigger.
description.consumes_meaning: Schedule ops (add/modify/remove/trigger by schedule_id) as body.op or as a tool_call turn.
examples: 22:00 UTC = 00:00 CEST -> the close pass runs its first sweep of the night
op trigger with the schedule_id -> the same firing, now, without changing the plan
